_comment: vendor/ is COMMITTED, so these patches normally ride along with it. They are
stored here because vendor/ is also regenerated wholesale on every platform
upgrade (npm install into a staging dir, then robocopy over vendor/node_modules),
which would silently drop them and reintroduce the bugs they fix.
Run `.smoke/platform-patches.py verify` after refreshing vendor/, and `apply`
to put them back. pack.py runs verify before packaging, so an unpatched tree
cannot be shipped. ExpectedPackageVersion guards against applying a patch to a
different upstream release: apply refuses unless the installed version matches.

why: The released-v0 validators are exact and the v0->v1 migration refuses a
Session carrying anything outside the released shape. Correct for the
released format, but this deployment bakes third-party plugins that wrote
into sessions freely, and one offending event makes a whole session
unobservable. On a real 30-session history the strict validators refused
1251 events across 21 sessions, in four shapes:
1. a content block with a plugin annotation (dsh-file-review's
`dshFileReview` on an empty text block appended to a tool result);
2. a kind:'plugin' source with an extra member (dsh-web-review's
`snapshotId`);
3. a kind:'plugin' source pairing `summary` with a non-notice form
(dsh-mnemon's `instructions` + summary);
4. `subagent/descriptor` version 2 from the `sidechat` plugin, where the
released spec froze on version 3.
The patch drops (1)(2)(3)'s unreleased members and the stray summary, and
coerces (4)'s version 2 to 3, each logged once. Required members, missing
members and unknown kinds still refuse, and the source v0 artifact is never
modified.
Restores the embedded 'open configuration file' bridge, which 0.1.5 deleted
along with dsh-host-apiproxy.
In 0.1.1 that package's settings handler ran `if (DSH_EMBEDDED === "1")`
and wrote `[dsh-vscode:open-settings] <path>` on stdout so the containing VS
Code extension could reveal the document in its own editor, because the
native opener is invisible in an embedded deployment. 0.1.5 moved settings
to dsh-api-settings-controller, which calls openTextFile UNCONDITIONALLY —
the env check and the sentinel are gone, and openSettingsDocument (unlike
openAgentPresetDirectory) has no 'return the path instead' branch. Nothing
in 0.1.5 reads DSH_EMBEDDED at all (the only DSH_* env seams left are
DSH_AGENTS_HOME, DSH_BUNDLED_SKILL_DIR, DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED,
DSH_WEB_FETCH_PROVIDER and DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER), so there is no official
seam to use instead: the panel's 'open configuration file' silently did
nothing after the upgrade.
The patch re-adds the branch in the handler that took over the same job, and
leaves the internals.openTextFile seam intact (asserted by
.smoke/embedded-open-settings-test.mjs, which drives the real controller
with stubbed internals both with and without DSH_EMBEDDED=1).
Stops a console window from appearing for the lifetime of every command.
launchWindowsJob is the path Windows normally takes: it spawns the managed
job runner with
child = (internals.spawn ?? spawn)(command, [...prefix, '--', ...argv], {
cwd, env, stdio: runnerStdio(...)
and no windowsHide. Windows therefore gives that runner a fresh console, so
a terminal window pops up when a command starts and closes when it finishes.
The omission is upstream's, and visibly an oversight: the FALLBACK path in the
same package, spawnSubprocess, already passes
`windowsHide: platform === 'win32'` beside `detached: platform !== 'win32'`.
Only the primary Windows path forgot it. The option is ignored off Windows, so
the patch is inert on Linux and macOS.
Found by auditing every child_process call site in the tree for windowsHide
rather than grepping for it: this call is written
`(internals.spawn ?? spawn)(`, so a pattern anchored on `spawn(` misses it, and
the file-level question 'does this file mention windowsHide' also misses it
because the taskkill calls in the same package do set it.
Makes Archived Tasks readable again on this platform.
The bundled @dsh-undo/* plugins were built against a newer persistence
contract whose service exposes inspect(id). This backend does not, so every
archived — that is, non-live — session failed with
sessionArchive.list failed gateway/internal:
this.ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect is not a function
Live sessions never reach it: the callers prefer
`ctx.sessions.get(id)?.events` and only fall back to persistence for sessions
with no live handle, which is exactly the archived set.
The service class itself is a bare `class extends Service { constructor }` in
the base package; the methods live in this jsonl backend, whose API is
locate/create/open/flush/stat/list/requireStoredLog. The patch adds
inspect(id, options) on top of `open(id, 'read')` + `handle.read()`, so it
introduces no new storage behavior, and callers only read `.events`.
Asserted behaviorally, not textually, by .smoke/persistence-inspect-test.mjs:
it imports the real module and checks inspect is a 2-arity function on the
prototype, plus that open/list/locate still exist (otherwise inspect would be
dead code even while defined).
Two console-visibility defects, both measured rather than guessed at.
(1) The ordinary Job path. launchWindowsJob spawns the managed runner, and on
Windows that spawn carried no windowsHide, so the runner got a fresh console - a
terminal window for the lifetime of every command. The fallback in the same
package (spawnSubprocess) already passed windowsHide: platform === "win32"; this,
the path Windows normally takes, simply omitted it. Fixed with an unconditional
windowsHide: true (ignored off Windows).
(2) The confined (restricted-token) path - the one every sandboxed command goes
through, and the reason the symptom came back after (1) was fixed. A runtime trace
of ONE `powershell -NoProfile -Command "echo hi"` ends at
CreateProcessAsUserW(flags=4) inside spawnInheritedJobProcess, and the
STARTUPINFOW handed to it had `dwFlags: 256` (STARTF_USESTDHANDLES only). The
`wShowWindow: 0` sitting right beside it was INERT, because Windows only honours
wShowWindow when STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW is set; and since the VS Code host is
Electron/Code.exe - a GUI binary, for which CREATE_NO_WINDOW/windowsHide is
ignored - the sandbox runner owns no console to inherit, so Windows allocated a
VISIBLE one for the confined child: a black window for the lifetime of every
sandboxed command. Fixed exactly the way the dsh-silent-pwsh plugin does it: set
STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW on both STARTUPINFOW sites (dwFlags 256 -> 257) so SW_HIDE
takes effect (wShowWindow: 0 added on the piped site, already present but inert on
the job site).
DELIBERATELY NOT CREATE_NO_WINDOW on that path: the DSH maintainers verified that
under the restricted token it makes the child die with STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED
(0xC0000142). It did pass one local workspace-write run here (exit 0, stdout
intact, no window), which is exactly the kind of environment-dependent breakage
not worth shipping - a command that dies is worse than a flash. For the same
reason dsh-silent-pwsh uses SW_HIDE.
Verified: .smoke/windows-hide-test.mjs now asserts the shape (both dwFlags: 257,
both wShowWindow: 0, no dwFlags: 256 left, no CREATE_NO_WINDOW on the restricted
call sites) AND runs a real workspace-write confined command end to end: exit 0,
stdout intact, and no new visible window or console-host process.
Fork seed must not swallow the next user/message after the cut turn.
Original loop advanced cut until turn/start, so a queued next prompt
was included in the child; the agent then auto-ran it and the user's
new send was queued behind it. Also patched lib/types/commands.js
with the same cut logic (duplicate host fork implementation).
Duplicate fork implementation of the same cut loop; kept in sync with lib/index.js LOCAL PATCH.
The one-time windows-acl capability probe spawns the confinement runner around
`cmd /c exit 0` with a bare { timeout, stdio: "ignore" } - no windowsHide - so
that probe can flash a console window on the first host start, exactly like the
per-command spawns did. Same omission, same fix: windowsHide: true. Found by
diffing our patch set against the dsh-silent-pwsh plugin, which patches this
site too; our earlier per-file audit missed it because the file already mentions
windowsHide elsewhere (the bwrap probe), which is precisely the trap the
explore.27 note warns about.
